(Owner of Tipper Lorry bearing No.KA42A2957) (Exparte) *J U D G M E N T*
This judgment is emerged consequent upon the petition filed by the petitioner, U/S 166 of Motor Vehicles Act, claiming compensation of Rs.5,00,000/, on account of damage to the vehicle bearing registration No.KA41N8877, in a road traffic accident.
*FACTS OF THE CASE IN NUTSHELL*
2. Facts leading to the case of the petitioner forthcoming in the petition that, on 11.3.2017, the petitioner was travelling in a Swift Car bearing registration No.KA41 N8877, from Bengaluru to Malemahadeshwar Temple.

At about 8.00 a.m., when the said car reached near Bank of Baroda, B.M.Road, Vandaraguppe Village,
Channapatna Taluk, at that time, the driver of the Tipper Lorry bearing registration No.KA42A2957, driven the same in a rash and negligent manner with high speed and dashed to the petitioner's car.
As a result, the car of the petitioner was damaged.
3. It is further stated in the petition that, the petitioner had purchased the said car in model 2011, and since then he had maintained it in good condition.

Due to the accident, the bumper, engine bonnet, front side fender, right side head light, right side door, right side body, right side wheel, rear bumper, rear right side tail lamp and indicators of the car were damaged.
4. It is alleged in the petition that, the said car purchased from Kalyani Motors Pvt.
Ltd, Channapatna,
and he left the said car, for repair for about two months and paid parking charges to the said garage.
He spent more than Rs.5,00,000/ towards vehicle repair charges and other charges.
He used car/taxi for rent basis for the purpose of his real estate business for a period of three months.

5. Further stated that, the jurisdictional Channapatana traffic police have registered the criminal case, in connection with the accident in question, in Cr.No.35/2017, against the driver of the offending vehicle, for the offences punishable under section 279 of I.P.C.

As such, the respondent No.1 being the insurer and the respondent No.2, being the owner of the offending vehicle are jointly and severally liable to pay compensation to the petitioner, towards the damages caused to the Sri.C.Manohar vs ) Royal Sundaram General on 16 February, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/144802499/
2 vehicle in question, belonged to the petitioner.
6. After registration of the case, as usual notices were issued to the respondents.

In response to the notices, the respondent No.1 made its appearance through counsel and filed the written statement,
in answer to the case of the petitioner.
On the other hand, the respondent No.2 has not appeared before the Court, remained absent and placed exparte.
7. In the written statement of the respondent No.1, has denied the accident and the involvement of the Lorry in the accident.
Further admitted about issuance of insurance policy in respect of Lorry bearing registration No.KA42A2957, in favour of respondent No.2, subjected to the terms and conditions of the policy.

Further contended that, neither owner of the offending vehicle nor the jurisdictional police have complied the mandatory provisions of Section 134(2) and Section 158(6)
of Motor Vehicles Act in furnishing better particulars.
Further contended that, driver of insured lorry was not holding a valid and effective driving licence at the time of accident.
And also the offending vehicle was not having valid permit and FC to ply in the place of accident.

It is the contention of respondent that, the car bearing registration No.KA41N8877 was duly insured with a package policy, and upon the accident the petitioner has preferred the claim with his insurer ICCI Lombard General Insurance Co. Ltd., and received the amount towards damages in full and final settlement from his insurer.

entities.text: ICCI Lombard General Insurance Co. Ltd.
entities.label: ORG

sentences.text: Hence, the petitioner is estopped from maintaining the present petition.
With all these main grounds, prayed to dismiss the petition against their company.

8. On the basis of the rival pleadings of both the parties, for final determination of this case,
following issues were framed:
*ISSUES*
1.

Whether the petitioner proves that, his Swift Car bearing registration No.KA41 N 8877 has damaged in an accident, that occurred on 11.03.2017 at about 8.00 a.m.,
near Bank of Baroda, B.M. Road, Vandaraguppe village, Channapatna Taluk, due to the rash and negligent driving of the driver of the Tipper Lorry bearing Regn. No.KA 42A2957 ?
2. Whether the petitioner is entitled for compensation as prayed for? If so, at what rate?

From whom?
3.
What order or award?
9. In order to substantiate its case, the petitioner C.Manohar, during the course of evidence, placed his affidavit evidence in lieu of examination inchief, who examined as PW1.
At the time of his evidence, placed his affidavit evidence and 13 documentary evidence got marked as Ex.P1 to Ex.P13.
In addition to this, placed the evidence of PW2 N.Madhava.
At the time of his evidence, documents got marked as Ex.P.14 to Ex.P.16.

On the other hand, to prove the defenses of the respondent No.1,
placed the evidence of Nayaz, Team Leader / OD Claim Manager of ICICI Lombard Insurance Company as RW1.
At the time of his evidence, three documents got marked as Ex.R1 to Ex.R.3.

3
After completion of the trial, matter was set down for arguments.
10. Heard the arguments of both the counsel.
And perused the materials available on record.

11. Consequently, on appreciation of the evidence available on record, my findings to the aforesaid issues are as follows:
 Issue No.1: In the Affirmative.

Issue No.2: Partly in the Affirmative.
 Issue No.3:

As per final order,
 for the following:
 R E A S O N S  ISSUE NO.1:
12.

It is my humble opinion that, since the facts of the case has been narrated in detail above, once again, narration of the assertion of the petitioner and the defenses' of the respondent No.1 forthcoming in the written statement is not required herein.

13. Firstly, in connection with ownership of the vehicle bearing registration No.KA41N8877 is concerned, in the evidence of PW1C.Manohar in para No.2 & 3 of his affidavit evidence, narrated about the accident and the damages caused to his vehicle in question.
In support of all the averments made in the affidavit of the petitioner placed R.C. and D.L. along with his Aadhar card, to prove the ownership of the vehicle in question.
The said documents remained unquestioned by the other side.
Though the other side placed the evidence of RW1, team leader of O.D. claim department of Insurance company, not denied the ownership of the petitioner in connection with the vehicle in question.
14. Further, the petitioner to show that, in the accident in question occurred on the fateful day of the 11.3.2017, his vehicle was damaged, placed the police documents as per Ex.P1 to Ex.P5.

On going through the recitals of the said documents, reveal that, on the basis of first information given by the petitioner himself, on the same date of the accident, against the driver of the offending vehicle bearing registration No.KA42A2957 Tipper Lorry, case was registered, against the driver of the said lorry, alleging that, he has committed the offence punishable under section 279 of IPC.

In the recitals of the complaint, and the Ex.P1, and also in the mahazar marked at Ex.P3, said to have executed in presence of panch witnesses, and the report of the motor vehicle inspector marked at Ex.P.4, speak about the genuineness of the case of the petitioner, about the involvement of the offending vehicle, in the accident, and the damages caused to him vehicle consequent upon the accident.
Added to this, final report submitted by the investigation marked at Ex.P.5 officer in connection with the accident and its consequences remained unquestioned by the other side.

In the Sri.C.Manohar vs ) Royal Sundaram General on 16 February, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/144802499/
4 column No.17 of the Ex.P5, there is a clear narration that, due to the negligence on the part of the driver of the offending vehicle, car belonged to the petitioner was damaged as fully noted in the report of the motor vehicle inspector as per Ex.P4.

sentences.text:
The recitals of the said material document,
remained unquestioned.

15. Apart from this, the PW1, during the course of his crossexamination clearly stated that, he purchased the vehicle in question in the year 2011, and he is the owner of the said vehicle having valid insurance policy as on the date of the accident from ICICI Lombard company, and also he answered that, with respect to the damages to his vehicle, he informed to the insurance company and also submitted the claim form.
Subsequently survey process had taken place in connection with the vehicle in question belonged to the petitioner.

And denied the suggestion of the other side that,
he filed false case against the offending vehicle, though alleged accident had taken place due to his own negligence, and also denied that, at the time of accident his vehicle was in the middle of the road, and he was sole responsible for the accident, but, to conceal the same, false case has been foisted against the driver of the offending vehicle.
16. In support of the case of the petitioner, placed the evidence of PW2.
The said witness gave evidence with respect to the production of job card retail invoices as per Ex.P15 & Ex.P16.
But not adduced any evidence in connection with the accident and cause for damages to the vehicle in question belonged to the petitioner.

And at the time of crossexamination of this witness, no material points culled out to disbelieve the point that, the petitioner was the owner of the offending vehicle, as on the date of the accident and his vehicle was damaged consequent upon the accident.

17. It is relevant to note that, for compensation filed U/S.166 of MV Act, 1988, the claimant has to prove the accident in question, and consequent damages, only on the touchstone of preponderance of probabilities and the standard of proof beyond reasonable doubt is not required, as held by Hon'ble Apex Court in the decision reported in, 2011 SAR (Civil) 319 (Kusum and others Vs. Satbir and others).

entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: " It was observed that, "When the accident, from the driver of the offending vehicle is proved, clearly indicates that, due to the said mistake on the part of the driver of the offending vehicle, the defending vehicle was damaged."

18. In the light of my due discussions held above, I am of the view that, the evidence of PW1 and the documentary evidence placed by the petitioner, along with the evidence of PW2, and the evidence of RW1, substantiate the case of the petitioner.

Hence, I am of the opinion that, petitioner has proved his stand that, the accident had occurred due to rash and negligent driving of the driver of the offending vehicle Tipper Lorry bearing registration No.KA42A2957.

In the said accident,
the defending vehicle Swift car, bearing registration No.KA41N8877, belonged to the petitioner was damaged.
Accordingly, I am answering the Issue No.1 is in the Affirmative.

ISSUE NO. 2:
Sri.C.Manohar vs ) Royal Sundaram General on 16 February, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/144802499/
5 19.

The petitioner being the owner of the defending vehicle bearing registration No.KA41N 8877, asserting herein that, after the accident, vehicle in question belonged to the petitioner was fully damaged.
And in toto, the petitioner had suffered a loss of Rs.5,00,000/.

In the evidence of PW1, in para No.3, clearly stated that, due to the accident, following damages were caused to the Swift Car bearing registration No.KA41N8877 noted as follows:
"front bumper damaged, Engine bannet damaged, front right side fender damaged,
right side head light damaged, right side door damaged, rear right side tail lamp and indicator damaged."

20. Further, he deposed that, in this regard, he left the said car for a period of two months, at Kalyani Motors Private Limited for the purpose of repairs and paid parking charges to the said garage.
Due to all these hardships, he spent more than Rs.5,00,000/ towards vehicle repair charges and other incidental charges.
Further, he noted in the affidavit that, when his vehicle was for repair, he used take private vehicle for hire, for his real estate business purpose for a period of three months.
As such, the respondent No.1 & 2, are liable to pay compensation to him.
21. In support of his stand, produced one advance bill as per Ex.P6, 2 final bill as per Ex.P7 and tyre purchase bill as per Ex.P8, along with photographs and CD as per Ex.P12 & Ex.P13.
In the Ex.P6 total repair charges were noted as Rs.23,050/.

In the Ex.P7 it is noted that, a sum of Rs.27,270/
and Rs.30,000/, Rs.27,270/ were received.
In the cash tag invoice total amount has been noted as Rs.6,700/.
Except these documents, no other documentary evidence is available on record for consideration from the side of the petitioner.
22. At the time of crossexamination of PW1, denied the suggestion of the other side that, after survey process, he received expenses from the company, and there was a final settlement.
And denied the suggestion that, after taking all the expenses of repairing of the vehicle, he submitted only copies to the court.
But admitted that, Ex.P6 and Ex.P7 are carbon copies by stating that, they were received from showroom.
Further, in para No.2 of his crossexamination stated that, he has not received any documents from the company to show that, he has not received any compensation amount from the company.
And also admitted that, he has not produced survey report along with estimation, and also not produced unclaimed notice sent by insurance company.
Subsequently, he has not produced the said material documents for consideration.

Further in para No.8 of his cross examination, denied the suggestion that, in collusion with the owner of the show room, he got repaired his vehicle with respect to the damages caused in the accident, including earlier damages of the vehicle.

23. Apart from this, on going through the documents placed by the PW2, as per Ex.P14 to Ex.P16,
job card retail invoice reveal about the net bill amount of Rs.1,41,912/.

At the time of his cross examination, he stated that, before repairing the vehicle, they enquired about the damages found in the vehicle in question, and also not denied the suggestion that, after enquiry of the vehicle damages, there will be a preparation of quotation list and the expenses list.
And answered that, if at all, there was any insurance to the said vehicle, they will inform to the insurance company.

And not denied the suggestion that, surveyor had submitted report, thereafter received work order from Sri.C.Manohar vs ) Royal Sundaram General on 16 February, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/144802499/
6 ICICI, and not denied the suggestion that, insurance company directly sent amount to their company and not denied the suggestion that, after receipt of full amount, there may be a process of giving endorsement in this regard.
24.

Added to this, in connection with the vehicle of the petitioner, in para No.2 admitted that, the vehicle in question was sent to their company for examination and denied the suggestion that, the damages noted in Ex.P15 & Ex.P16, belonged to their company, are contradictory with the recitals of Ex.P4.
And in continuation answered that, while giving Ex.P4, there was no deep enquiry with respect to the damages of the vehicle.

And stated that, before starting repair work, they have taken photographs of the vehicle, and in para No.3, he answered that, if at all there was 80% damages to the vehicle, they will suggest for repair of entire body of the vehicle in question.
25.
In answer to the evidence of PW1 & PW2, the respondent No.1 herein, placed the evidence of RW1 Nayaz, Team leader of ICICI Lombard Insurance Company.
At the time of his evidence, placed survey report, original claim form and estimation as per Ex.R1 to Ex.R3.
And in support of the said documents, he gave evidence that, for the purpose of repairing process of vehicle in question, a sum of Rs.84,215/ was paid from their company towards full settlement.
Before releasing the said amount, same was informed to the owner of the vehicle towards full and final settlement.
Ex.P7 is the original bill and the Xerox copy of the said document was given to them by Kalyani Motors.
As per the said document, total expenditure was Rs.1,41,912/.
Out of the said amount a sum of Rs.57,697/ was paid by the owner of the vehicle in question in cash.

On going through the recitals of the Ex.R1 to Ex.R3, supports the evidence of the RW1, to disprove the said documents, the petitioner has not placed contra documents, to impeach the recitals of the Ex.R1 to Ex.R3.
26.

At the time of crossexamination of this witness, stated that, by virtue of the documents he came to know about the loss caused to the vehicle belonged to the petitioner, due to the accidental damages and denied the suggestion that, the insurance company has not paid any amount to the petitioner, as stated in the examinationinchief.

To impeach the evidence given by RW1, the petitioner has not produced any satisfactory document on record to show that, the petitioner has not received any amount from the company and total loss caused to him was Rs.5,00,000/.
In the absence of material documents, about the definite loss, court cannot come to the conclusion with respect to the payment or definite damages on the basis of surmises and conjectures.
As per Ex.P16 net bill round off amount is at Rs.1,41,912/.
As per the evidence of RW1 the petitioner had received from the company a sum of Rs.84,215/ and remaining Rs.57,697/ was paid by the owner of the vehicle in cash.

By taking into consideration of all these aspects, and the damages noted in the Ex.P4, pertaining to the vehicle of the petitioner, damage of front bumper, engine bonnet, front right side pender, right side head light, right side door's, right side body, rear right side wheel, rear bumper, rear right side tail lamp and indicators.

And also by taking in to consideration of the hardship caused to the petitioner, while the said vehicle was sent for repairing process, I am of the view that, it is apt to award compensation of Rs.75,000/ towards damages of the vehicle.
The same will meet the ends of justice.

27. In the light of my detailed discussions held above, keeping in mind about the damages mentioned in the recitals of the IMV report, and also inconvenience caused to the petitioner, due to Sri.C.Manohar vs ) Royal Sundaram General on 16 February, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/144802499/
7 the said damage, I am of the view that, the petitioner is entitled for compensation of Rs.75,000/
(Rupees seventy five thousand only) along with interest @ 6% per annum, from the date of the petition, till the realization of the award amount.

LIABILITY:
28.
As regards to the liability is concerned, in the case on hand, accident has not been seriously disputed by the other side.

And the evidence given by the petitioner discloses that, due to the actionable negligence on the part of the driver of the offending vehicle Tipper Lorry registration No.KA 42A2957, alleged accident had taken place.
In the said accident, the defending vehicle Swift car bearing registration No.KA41N8877 belonging to the petitioner was damaged.
The respondent No.1 being the insurance company, has not denied the existence of the issuance of the policy with respect to the offending vehicle belonged to the respondent No.2.

And no evidence available on record, about the violation of the terms and conditions of the policy and also to prove the defence that, the driver of the offending vehicle had no valid and effective driving licence, no acceptable evidence is available on record.
On the other hand, in this regard, no whisper in the charge sheet submitted by the investigation officer, which remained unshaken.
29. As such, the respondent No.1 being the insurance company and the respondent No.2 being the owner of the offending vehicle, are jointly and severally liable to pay compensation to the petitioner.
However, the respondent No.1, being the insurance company and indemnifier has to satisfy the award.
In view of the valid insurance policy, the respondent No.1, is liable to pay the compensation with interest at 6% p.a. from the date of petition, till its realization.
Accordingly, I am answering the issue No.2 partly in the Affirmative.

ISSUE NO.3:
30.

In view of due discussions on issue Nos.1 & 2, I proceed to pass the following;
*O R D E R*
The petition filed by the petitioner U/s 166 of M.V. Act, is hereby partly allowed with cost.

Consequently, the petitioner is entitle for damages of Rs.75,000/ (Rupees seventy five thousand only) along with interest @ 6% per annum, from the date of the petition, till the realization of the award amount.
The respondent No.1 & 2 are jointly and severally liable to pay the award amount to the petitioner.

In view of the valid insurance policy, the respondent No.1 is liable to pay the compensation with interest at 6% p.a. from the date of petition till its realization within two months from the date of this order.
After deposit of the award amount with interest, since the compensation amount is meager, the entire amount shall be released to the petitioner through due process of law.

Advocate fee is fixed at Rs.500/.

8
